issues.legal_issue: A tenant is not disentitled to retain rented premises merely because the tenant’s spouse was allotted another residence, unless the tenant has a legal right or domain to occupy it and can reasonably use it as a substitute residence.
material_facts: The tenant’s wife was allotted government accommodation because of her employment as a teacher.
The rented premises were occupied by the tenant and his family, while the wife lived in the allotted accommodation.
The allotted accommodation was not the matrimonial home, and the tenant had no statutory or legal right to use or occupy it.
The wife later gave up her employment and returned to the rented premises.
The eviction petition relied on the wife’s allotment as the basis for eviction under the provision concerning acquisition or allotment of another residence.
issues.conclusion: The wife’s employment-related allotment did not disentitle the tenant to retain the rented premises because the tenant had no legal right or domain over the allotted residence and it was not available to him as a reasonable substitute. The eviction petition on that ground was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14(1)(h) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958 applies where the tenant himself builds, acquires vacant possession of, or is allotted another residence. The Act protects tenants from eviction, and this provision is an exception to that protection. A spouse’s acquisition or allotment is not automatically the tenant’s acquisition: the provision applies where the tenant has a legal right, by virtue of the spouse’s acquisition or allotment, to occupy the residence and can use it as an alternative to the rented premises. Smt. Revti Devi v. Kishan Lal supports the requirement that the tenant himself acquire the residence as of right. Prem Chand v. Sher Singh was distinguished because the other residence there was available to the tenant. Phiroze Bamanji Desai v. Chandrakant M. Patel and Gajanan Dattatraya v. Sherbanu Hosang Patel were treated as not governing this issue; the English matrimonial-home principles discussed in Halsbury’s Laws of England did not assist because equivalent rights were not granted in India.

rule.if: residential_tenancy_eviction_proceeding and eviction_sought_for_another_residence and spouse_only_received_allotment and tenant_lacks_legal_right_to_occupy and residence_not_reasonable_substitute

predicates.residential_tenancy_eviction_proceeding: A landlord pursued eviction of a residential tenant.
predicates.eviction_sought_for_another_residence: The landlord relied on the tenant having another residence as the ground for eviction.
predicates.spouse_only_received_allotment: The tenant’s spouse, rather than the tenant, received the allotment of the other residence.
predicates.tenant_lacks_legal_right_to_occupy: The tenant had no legal right or domain to occupy the residence allotted to the spouse.
predicates.residence_not_reasonable_substitute: The other residence was not reasonably available to the tenant as a substitute for the rented premises.

issues.definition: When eviction is sought on the basis of another residence in a residential tenancy proceeding, the tenant is not evictable on that ground if only the spouse received the allotment, the tenant lacks a legal right to occupy the residence, and it is not a reasonable substitute.

issues.legal_issue: Dismissal of an eviction claim based on acquisition or allotment of another residence does not determine or prejudice a separate eviction claim based on the landlord’s bona fide need.
material_facts: A separate eviction petition based on the landlord’s bona fide need remained pending when the appeal concerning the other-residence ground was decided.
The Court dismissed only the eviction petition based on the other-residence ground.
issues.conclusion: The dismissal did not prejudice the parties’ rights, if any, in the separate pending eviction petition based on bona fide need.
issues.legal_principle: The Court expressly limited its decision to the eviction ground based on acquisition or allotment of another residence and preserved the parties’ rights in the separate pending bona fide-need proceeding.

predicates.appeal_from_residential_eviction_order: A tenant appealed an order concerning eviction from residential premises.
predicates.separate_bona_fide_need_proceeding_pendi: A separate proceeding based on the landlord’s bona fide need remained pending.
predicates.current_eviction_ground_rejected: The eviction ground being considered in the appeal was rejected.

issues.definition: When an eviction ground is rejected on appeal while a separate bona fide-need proceeding remains pending, the separate claim is unaffected.
